$comment: LEVEL 3 -- DAGAT. Cross the sea and reach the next painting.
ONE JOURNEY WITH TWO FORKS, not three problems with three answers. Piyesta was
puzzle-dense and this is the change of rhythm after it: fewer branches, each one
longer. The shore teaches the new rule, the first fork splits the crossing, and both
sides arrive at the same encounter, which has three resolutions in two stagings.
THE FORK IS TWO OPTIONS AND SCORES ONE POINT, like every other fork in the game. The
design wanted the dive split half to pragmatist and half to protector; route_counts is
an integer dictionary compared against EndingResolver.ROUTE_COMMITMENT, and a half
point cannot be added to it. Boat is artist, dive is pragmatist, and Protector's
expression in this level is the fight at L3_N2 -- which is where the design says it
should be, because that is where it costs something.
WHAT IS NOT HERE YET: the boat route's traversal and its lore scene, the bakunawa's
surface staging, and the island. They are named in LEVEL_3.md as deferred, and the
reason is that every distance in them depends on numbers run_swim_reach_probe.gd only
just produced.
display_name_note: The hub plate says DAGAT and so does this. No second spelling to reconcile, unlike Piyesta.
goal: cross the sea, get past what is in it, and reach the next painting on the far sand

checkpoints.$comment: The design's own decision: 'a checkpoint sits partway through the encounter, so a reset costs the current stretch and not the whole approach. An encounter-length reset with no mid-point turns a five-minute section into twenty.' It serves both of the resolutions that can be lost -- contact while slipping past, and losing the fight.

THE ARRIVAL, and it is a checkpoint because every CheckpointArea2D in a scene must be declared here or the level errors at load. Reaching it past the encounter is what ends the level; the write is incidental.

$comment: ONE RULE, AND IT IS A CONSEQUENCE RATHER THAN A BAN. Piyesta refuses a bee at the
canvas; Dagat lets a horse be drawn, spawned and paid for, and then it cannot cope.
The design is explicit about why: 'a land creature spawned underwater should not be
silently refused -- let it flounder for a beat, have Lolo react, then revert it. The
refusal is funnier and clearer than a blocked draw.'
NO SIZE RULE AND NO FLIGHT CEILING HERE. Two levels in a row with a banned-class list
would read as a pattern of nagging rather than of place, and there are no bandaritas
to hang a ceiling from -- so if BANDARITAS_CUT lifted Piyesta's cap, this is the first
level where flight is simply unrestricted.

aquatic_only.armed_where: below the waterline only; the shore and the boat's deck are air

$comment: THE TUNING PASS. run_swim_reach_probe.gd measured all seven at 685-762 px per unit of
ink -- a 1.11x spread against the 3.8x the land probe found -- because swim_speed fell
back to the same 260 for everybody. The design asks outright for a fish to cost less to
hold than a shark, so the seven now differ on TWO axes and the axes pull against each
other, which is what makes the choice of body a choice:
sea_turtle  slow and cheapest   -- the endurance body; it crosses furthest per unit
fish        the baseline        -- unremarkable on purpose, and what the shore teaches
crab        slow and cheap      -- a land animal coping, and coping adequately
frog        quick and awkward   -- bursts, and it pays for them
octopus     middling both ways
penguin     fast and middling   -- genuinely a fast swimmer, and priced for it
shark       fastest, dearest    -- the sprint. Best reach per SECOND, worst per UNIT
The inversion is the point: the fastest class is not the one that gets furthest on a
budget. R10a in LEVEL_TEMPLATE.md says the slowest answer and the most expensive answer
stop being the same class once a drain exists, and this is that being true.
EVERY RATE IS CHECKED, NOT CHOSEN. run_swim_reach_probe.gd reads this block rather than
InkDrain's default and fails if any of the seven cannot cover the longest stretch
between refills. A body the level offers and cannot pay for is a dead end.
⚠ THREE OF THE SIX SIT INSIDE THE ARENA, AND ALL THREE ARE WEST OF THE COILS. Everything
before the encounter is priced in distance and comfortably covered; the encounter is priced
in time, and a shark holds a form for fifteen seconds on a full tank while one sweep of the
creature's cone takes almost eight. A fourth sat at 4250, behind the coils at 4230..4390 --
unreachable until the encounter is already over, and still counted toward the encounter's
budget, which is ink the player cannot spend. The one at 4050 is under the creature: going
into its space to pay for staying there is a trade worth offering.
ink_economy.zero_case: revert, carry the apo to the surface or the nearest air pocket, lose the crossing, never die

objectives.$comment: THE OBJECTIVE LINE, one per state of the run. level_3.gd decides which state the player is in; these are only the words, held to the same rule every dialogue line is held to: no line names a drawable class. Dangerous here in a way it was not in Piyesta -- the sea is full of classes. Never 'fish', 'shark', 'crab', 'sun', 'cloud', 'sailboat' or 'submarine'.
objectives.brush: Something in the sand is catching the light
objectives.practice: Try it in the shallows. Watch what it costs to stay changed
objectives.practice.tags: Draw something that can {tags} and take it into the shallows
objectives.cross.tags: Draw something that can {tags} — or walk the shore and see what is beached there
objectives.bakunawa: It cannot see. Decide what you are going to do about that
objectives.bakunawa.tags: Something that can {tags} — or slip by while it is looking elsewhere
objectives.island: Go up onto the far sand

$comment: A TUTORIAL BEAT DISGUISED AS A PICKUP, and the design is firm that it comes before
the fork: 'the player has spent two levels with a timer and now loses it, so the
shore has to teach the replacement before the fork, not after -- once they are
underwater, learning the ink rule by running out of it is a punishment, not a
lesson.'
THE BRUSH ITSELF IS NOT AN OBSTACLE. It is a pickup in the scene, because a sub-beat
resolves a tag and picking something up is not a drawing. It writes new_brush and
the drain arms from there.
ONE SUB-BEAT, AND IT IS AT THE WATERLINE rather than on dry sand. That way the
practice teaches the drain AND puts a Swim body in the player's hands before L3_N1
asks for one, which is what teaches_before_choice is for. Failure is not possible:
the shallows are not deep enough to lose anything in.
TWO ROUTES, NOT THREE, and that is the design rather than an omission: 'you need to
go to the sea, what do you choose? TWO CHOICES ONLY.' DialogueChoiceOverlay skips a
missing route rather than drawing a blank button -- L2_N3 is the precedent -- so
this renders two buttons end to end.
THE BOAT IS FOUND, NOT DRAWN. The design decided it: 'found fits the artist framing
-- the artist path in Level 2 was also about looking and asking rather than making.'
So the route declares answered_by and is closed with director.solve_with_item, which
is what keeps a class nobody drew out of the per-class precision and recall figures.

artist.$comment: The boat gets how he died. The apo is seated and rowing, with nothing to do but listen -- the only scene in the game where they cannot draw their way out of a conversation.

pragmatist.$comment: Seven answers. The dive gets what it did to lola, told while the apo swims away from him and cannot look at him, which is its own kind of scene and does something the boat version cannot.

$comment: ONE ENCOUNTER, THREE RESOLUTIONS, TWO STAGINGS. Both routes arrive here, so it is
written once. A blind creature, frantic, searching for something it lost, with eyes
Lolo half-recognises: the encounter is built as a portrait of lola's grief and every
resolution is a way of treating it. Helping it see, it finds what it was looking
for. Avoiding it, it keeps searching. Fighting it, you win against something that
was never attacking you on purpose.
THE FLOWER COMES FROM THE LIGHT AND NOT FROM THE FIGHT, deliberately.
THE BAKUNAWA IS AN AUTHORED ENCOUNTER, not one of the fifty drawable classes and not
a mythology mechanic -- the same framing as the aswang in Dilim. Worth a line in the
thesis chapter, since a bakunawa that eats the moon is the association a reader will
bring.

artist.$comment: Three answers, which is one above the floor -- and the floor is not a margin. It follows the light, uncovers what it was looking for, and gives up the flower gladly. The design asks that what it uncovers be something the player recognises rather than a generic chest.

pragmatist.$comment: NOT A DRAWING, so it declares answered_by like the dance did. Light cones from the bakunawa, shadow is safe, contact resets to CP3b. On the boat route it is not a dive -- the player steers wide and stays out of its sweep, same logic, same light-and-shadow rule, and the boat is not abandoned mid-level. A player who drew a flashlight and then chose this has made it harder for themselves, which the design says to allow rather than prevent.

protector.$comment: Five answers, and they already differ in more than damage: UtilityObject gives swing 96px, boomerang 320px, cannon 640px and the anvil a drop, which is exactly the differentiation the design asks for. Subdued or exhausted, NEVER killed -- it swims off still blind and still searching, and the cost of this route is that nothing was healed. Losing restarts the fight; it does not end the run.

hidden_flowers.$comment: THE THIRD OF FIVE, and unlike Payyo's it is not gated on a later level's tag -- it is this level's Artist-tagged reward, which is the rule the Dagat design sets for every level from here. The id here is documentation; the runtime id is what record_collectible is called with, and it must match PlayerProfile.FLOWER_IDS or the flower counts for nothing.

heard_how_he_died.does: suppresses the island's retelling of that half, because the boat already told it
heard_how_he_died.does_not: change which half the island delivers -- whichever the player has NOT heard lands there in full

heard_about_lola.does: the same, for the other half
heard_about_lola.does_not: gate anything; no player leaves Dagat without the whole of it

has_flower_3.does: shows it going into the satchel at the island, beside Piyesta's
has_flower_3.does_not: say what the flowers are for -- a secret ending that announces its requirements is not secret

cultural_constraints.$comment: Dagat has no sacred site in it the way Piyesta's plaza did, but it has a creature out of folk belief, and the guardrail is about how that creature is used rather than about what may be touched.

bakunawa.note: It is an authored encounter and a portrait of grief, not a bestiary entry and not a puzzle about folklore. The game never explains it, never names what its eyes remind Lolo of, and never lets the player kill it. The moon is not mentioned: the association a reader brings is the eclipse myth, and this is not that story.

the_death.note: The game stays with what the apo would actually understand -- that lola forgets -- rather than naming a condition or claiming grief caused it. The original design line is kept as intent; the script does not say the word.
